Data Services Platform
Introduction

Defra group have put in place the Data Services Platform to make environmental data openly available to a wide range of users. The more people know about the environment, the better informed will be their actions and decisions that can help safeguard our natural environment, support our food and farming industry and sustain a thriving rural economy. All our data can also be found in the data.gov.uk catalogue.

Data and services

Our data feeds ensure you are using the most up to date data, but nearly all of our data is also available for download in commonly used formats. Much of our data is spatial and can be readily used in GIS applications. But we also provide data via API Portal, built on Linked Data, which are aimed at system and application developers. We use the same open APIs and spatial services available to you to provide our own applications. But others can innovate, use and deliver our information in different ways, raising environmental awareness much further than we can do acting alone.

Partners

Although we make our data openly available when we can, certain data we hold has third party rights that mean we can only provide it to certain partner organisations or to contractors working for us on specific projects. If you are a partner or a Defra group contractor you can create an account to access additional data.

Defra Data Services Platform (DSP) – Fair Use Policy
1. Purpose

We provide the Defra Data Services Platform (DSP) to support decision-making, innovation, and public benefit. This policy is designed to keep the platform reliable and responsive for everyone.

While we encourage legitimate high-volume use, unchecked automation can slow the service for other users. These rules help us protect platform performance and ensure fair access.

2. General Principles

By using the DSP, you agree to:

Act Lawfully: Use data only for lawful purposes. You must not infringe on the rights of others or prevent them from using the platform.

Respect Licences: Most data is available under the Open Government Licence (OGL) v3.0. However, some datasets contain third-party rights (e.g., Ordnance Survey, UK Centre for Ecology and Hydrology data, as well as some Defra Group datasets.)

It is your responsibility to always check the licence terms in the dataset metadata.

If there is a conflict, specific dataset terms or contracts take precedence over this policy.

3. Permitted Use

You are free to:

Use and adapt OGL-licensed data for personal or commercial purposes, provided you credit the source.

Build applications and services using DSP data and APIs.

Share derived outputs, subject to relevant licence terms.

4. Automated Access and Rate Limits

"Automated access" refers to using the DSP via software, scripts, APIs, or system-to-system processes rather than a web browser.

To prevent overloading the platform, we apply rate limits.

At the time of publication, the current limits are:

Standard users: Up to 200 requests per minute.

Automated services such as system to system API calls: Up to 200 requests per minute.

Web bots including crawlers, scrapers, etc: Up to 10 requests per minute.

We monitor and may change these limits to ensure stability. If you are building a service that genuinely requires higher capacity, please contact us to discuss your requirements.

5. Prohibited Actions

requests that degrade performance for others.

Misrepresent Data: Do not present data in a misleading way or imply Defra endorses your product or conclusions.

Breach Third-Party Rights: Do not redistribute third-party data (e.g., Ordnance Survey) beyond what their specific licence allows.

Compromise Security: Do not attempt to bypass authentication, evade usage controls, or disrupt the service.

We reserve the right to match coordinated API calls to enforce the requests when they may appear to come from different users. Do not employ multiple IP addresses and/or user agents to avoid limitations described in 4. Automated Access and Rate Limits.

6. Registration and Privacy

If you hold a registered account (e.g., partner or contractor access):

Keep your credentials secure and notify us immediately of any breach.

Use the data only for the agreed purpose (e.g., fulfilling a contract).

Personal data processing is governed by Defra’s Privacy Policy. You must not attempt to re-identify individuals from anonymised data.

7. Attribution

When sharing, reusing, or creating derived data from DSP, you must:

Include the attribution statement found in the dataset metadata.

Clearly indicate if you have modified the original data.

8. Service Status and Liability

We provide DSP services and data "as is." We do not guarantee the service will be uninterrupted or error-free. We are not responsible for loss or damage resulting from your use of the platform, to the extent permitted by law.

9. Enforcement

We aim to act proportionately. However, if you breach this policy, we may:

Issue a warning.

Temporarily restrict or throttle your traffic.

Block automated traffic that is harming the platform.

Suspend or terminate access for serious or repeated misuse.

10. Policy Review

This policy is currently in a trial phase. We will review the rate limits and rules after 1, 3, and 6 months to ensure they are working for our users. By continuing to use the DSP, you agree to any updates.

11. Contact

You may contact DSP Support to request a review of any access restriction. For questions on licensing, access, or limits, please contact us via DSP Support.

Turning off the legacy Water Quality Archive
Turning off the legacy Water Quality Archive

Created: 27 Nov 2025 Updated: 27 Nov 2025

The old Water Quality Archive will be permanently retired from 11 December 2025.

 

If you were using the API from this service, you will need to access the data through the new URL. Details how to transition it are below.

 

The old URL will redirect to the new service so there is no need to update your bookmarks.

 

Transitioning to the new API

As the API has been redeveloped to use FAIR and Linked Data principles, there are some differences to note between the legacy API and the new service.

Paginated response

The new API is paginated, meaning that data is now returned in pages and with appropriate size limits. To obtain all data, your application will need to request multiple pages one after another.

Endpoint

	

Limit




/data/sampling-point

	

CSV/JSON: 2500 results per page

JSON-LD/GeoJSON: 250 results per page




/data/observation

	

All formats: 250 results per page

Removed features

Some features from the legacy API have been retired to improve precision and performance:

Legacy Feature

	

Alternative




year parameter

	

Use dateFrom and dateTo for precise date ranges




URL suffixes (.csv, .json)

	

Use Accept headers for content negotiation




_limit, _offset parameters

	

Use limit and skip parameters




/id/ endpoint prefix

	

Use direct resource paths




_view parameter

	

API optimizes response content automatically




_sorted parameter

	

Use client-side sorting for better performance




Batch download API

	

Use streaming formats (CSV, JSON Lines) with pagination

Updated endpoints

Terminology and endpoints have been updated in line with SOSA standards:

Legacy Endpoint

	

New Endpoint




/id/sampling-point

	

/data/sampling-point




/data/measurement

	

/data/observation




/data/sample

	

/sampling-point/{id}/sample




/def/determinands

	

/codelist/determinand




/def/units

	

/codelist/unit

Legacy Parameter

	

New Parameter

dateFrom=2015-01-01&dateTo=2015-12-31

easting/northing/radius

Limits to the number of sampling points in any given query

Each API query can include a maximum of 100 sampling points. This limit is enforced to prevent exceeding the allowable URL length for query parameters.
